summary: Weekly POC sync focused on validating operator runbook, quantization tuning impact on tail latency, and egress-run routing behavior. Agreed immediate next steps: share runbook, run two controlled latency benchmarks, and consolidate kernel/quant compatibility notes. Discussed fallback routing and KMS/access gating for private deployment.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-09
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Carlos (Redwood CSM), Samir (TelosHealth PM), Lena (NetEng), Rajiv (SecOps), Priya (SRE)

[00:00] Maya: alright everybody, thanks for hopping on. quick note, we'll run through runbook validation, quant tuning results from the canary, and then egress/routing behavior — and end with clear action items. sound good?
[00:24] Samir: yeah sounds good, thanks Maya. we've got Jen out today so i'm covering final scheduling.
[00:45] Ethan: i'll kick off with the kernel compatibility quick recap then show the latest perf numbers — fair?
[00:52] Lena: yep — and i have a couple net topo questions buried in the middle.

-- Runbook / Canary validation --
[01:10] Maya: ok Ethan?
[01:15] Ethan: sure, so last week's canary used quant profile Q3 (8-bit symmetric) on two replica pools — one ashore in the private VPC and one in the hosted fallback. overall token throughput held, but we did see a tail p99 increase on long context requests, roughly +18% compared to baseline. that was mostly in requests that exceed 2.5k tokens.
[01:46] Priya: can you repeat that? p99 went up on long ones only?
[01:49] Ethan: correct, short inference paths (<=512 tokens) are unaffected, low-latency preserved. the regression looks linked to KV cache handling in the quantized path — small extra decode iterations.
[02:10] Samir: ok that fits with the sample logs we saw — a few outliers around heavy multi-chunk conversations.
[02:22] Rajiv: any sign of increased error rates or OOMs?
[02:25] Ethan: none in the canary, memory stayed within thresholds. CPU on the host side bumped slightly due to extra iteration work, but not alarming.
[02:33] Maya: and we had the canary fallback trigger once, right?
[02:37] Ethan: yes around 09:42 UTC we saw one automated fallback to hosted variant, triggered by the latency SLI policy; routing rules worked as expected.
[02:46] Lena: this is where i want to confirm egress shaping — when fallback happens, are we still egressing through our private NAT or will traffic route via Redwood's hosted egress? we need to know for compliance.
[03:02] Maya: good question — currently fallback to hosted routes through Redwood's egress in the region. for the Private deployment we can configure a policy to keep egress in-customer VPC (forced local) but it requires the onprem bridge to be up. that was not present in the canary.
[03:20] Priya: so we had one fallback and it went out through hosted egress, which is not allowed for our PCI-scope workloads. that's a red flag for us.
[03:28] Maya: understood. that's why today's runbook validation is important — we want to make sure fallback behavior is explicit and we provide an emergency canary rollback path that doesn't egress.

-- Kernel / Quant compatibility --
[04:00] Ethan: about compatibility — we tested kernels v2.11 and v2.12. v2.12 has a micro-optimization that helps cache reuse but it also changes scheduling slightly. with Q3 quant we observed the p50 unchanged, p95 slightly better on v2.12, p99 regressed on long contexts. my recommendation is to pin v2.11 for the upcoming pilot week while we iterate on Q3 tweaks.
[04:34] Samir: is pinning feasible without losing performance for typical shorter queries?
[04:38] Ethan: yes, v2.11 is stable and gives predictable tail behavior — the difference in short-hit throughput is <3% in our tests.
[04:44] Lena: are the kernel differences documented somewhere? the ops team needs a matrix to approve images.
[04:49] Ethan: i'll share the compatibility sheet after this call. it'll list kernel, quant profile, and expected p95/p99 deltas per context-length bucket.
[04:57] Maya: add that to action items.

-- Telemetry & Observability --
[05:20] Carlos: quick note on telemetry — we added two new traces for KV cache hits and for quant-conversion time. you should see them in the telemetry dashboard in about an hour.
[05:31] Priya: cool — will that let us separate decode vs kv latency?
[05:34] Carlos: yes, that's the idea. decode, kv-lookup, and net RTT will be separate spans.

-- Networking specifics --
[06:00] Lena: we've been doing some packet captures during the canary and noticed occasional MTU path issues across the bridge. sometimes fragmentation spikes show up and add ~20-40ms. could those explain some p99 blips?
[06:16] Ethan: possible — if fragmentation causes retransmits and TCP waits, it could push the tail. do you have capture slices we can look at?
[06:21] Lena: yes i uploaded two samples to the shared drive: capture_canary_1102.pcap and capture_canary_1103.pcap.
[06:29] Samir: i saw those too — looks like at 10:03 we had a small queue buildup on our firewall. Priya, was there any scheduled maintenance?
[06:38] Priya: nope, nothing scheduled. i will check the host metrics for that window.

-- Incident simulation & rollback runbook --
[07:00] Maya: i want to validate the abort and rollback steps in the runbook. step 1 is detect, step 2 determine whether to fallback, step 3 execute fallback, step 4, if fallback violates egress policy, rollback to previous image. can we walk through a failure case?
[07:19] Ethan: sure. detection triggered at 09:40; policy looked at sliding p99 over 3m and error rate. fallback happened; for cases where egress is restricted we have a gating flag — "force-local-egress" — it prevents routing to hosted endpoints but will reduce capacity. for that we try scale-up first, if scale-up fails then we revert quant profile and kernel to previous stable.
[07:44] Rajiv: how do we ensure KMS keys are not used by hosted fallback? exfil risk.
[07:49] Maya: hosted fallback cannot access customer-managed KMS. we supply a note: hosted uses Redwood-managed KMS unless you configure a VPC-only fallback. we'll add explicit language in the runbook.
[07:58] Rajiv: need that in writing — and an architectural diagram.

-- Customer-run benchmarks discussed --
[08:20] Samir: plan is to run two benchmark windows: a daytime test with production-like concurrency and one overnight stress test. we'll push traffic through the private pool only and compare p50/p95/p99 versus the hosted baseline.
[08:33] Priya: i'll schedule those windows and share the ingress token and traffic profile.
[08:36] Maya: great, and Redwood will provide a synthetic workload spec to match.

[09:00] Ethan: small note on quant tuning — Q3 reduces model size by ~40% and lowers per-token cost; however those long-context regressions are real. we've got a preliminary Q3a tweak (slightly different scaling factor on activation quant) which in internal tests smoothed the p99 by ~9% on long contexts. it's not run in the canary yet.
[09:28] Samir: we'd prefer to try Q3a in a dark canary (no fallback) first if possible.
[09:33] Ethan: we can do that, yes — dark canary in the private pool only, monitor for 6 hours.

-- Observability and alerts --
[10:00] Carlos: for alerts we recommend adding a composite alert: p99 latency OR kv-cache-miss-rate OR host CPU spike for 5m. that would trigger the runbook start.
[10:12] Priya: make sure alert routing goes to our on-call Slack channel + the SE on-call.
[10:18] Maya: we'll add an alert playbook with runbook hyperlink and SE contact.

-- Small transcription hiccups / side chatter --
[10:40] (crosstalk) Lena: sorry interru — the firewall showed a bump, i think a new rule hit the queue, hold on.
[10:48] Priya: i see it, one sidecar pod dropped traffic for a minute while it rotated, might be related.

-- Security / Compliance note --
[11:10] Rajiv: on compliance, we need confirmation that log retention and audit trails for private events remain within our S3 bucket and are not mirrored to Redwood-hosted buckets. we need an assurance doc.
[11:22] Maya: understood — we'll share the compliance matrix and a short doc that explains what stays on-customer and what Redwood stores.
[11:31] Rajiv: also SSO mapping — is SAML enforced for the console in private mode?
[11:35] Maya: yes, private console supports SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning; we'll attach the config sample.

-- Deep-dive: Egress shaping & policy variations --
[12:05] Lena: a couple config questions: if we set force-local-egress true, what's the expected capacity reduction?
[12:12] Ethan: depends on peering throughput; our estimate from the canary is a 15-25% throughput hit under high concurrency because some batching is less efficient when you keep traffic local.
[12:22] Priya: is that 15-25% at p50 or p99?
[12:25] Ethan: throughput capacity — that percent reduction shows up on sustained throughput numbers; tail latency can worsen if the bridge is saturated.
[12:32] Samir: ok so for PCI workloads we'll probably prefer a conservative approach: force-local during business hours, allow controlled hosted fallback overnight if needed.
[12:42] Maya: we can template a policy like that in the runbook.

-- Questions from customer --
[13:00] Samir: can Redwood provide a small script to flip the quant profile and kernel atomically as part of rollback? manual steps increase risk.
[13:08] Ethan: yes, we have a CLI tool that can flip profiles and restart the runtime in a rolling fashion. we'll attach an example script.
[13:14] Priya: will that cause partial disruption?
[13:17] Ethan: rolling restarts are designed to keep capacity available — small blips possible but under the rollback plan we prefer that over a full fallback which may egress.

-- Mid-call lull / informal check --
[14:00] (10 second pause)
[14:12] Carlos: quick ops note — look for a new dashboard called "kv-quant-latency" in your org view. should be live in ~45 minutes.

-- Final alignment & scheduling --
[15:00] Maya: let's align on the timeline — Ethan will share the kernel/quant matrix by end of day tomorrow (2027-11-11). Maya will send the runbook draft and policy templates by 2027-11-12. Priya will book benchmark windows for 2027-11-14 and 2027-11-15. Rajiv will send SOC2 scoping questions by 2027-11-15. does that match people's expectations?
[15:24] Samir: yes that's fine.
[15:27] Lena: fine for me.
[15:30] Rajiv: yep.

-- Recap and close --
[15:40] Maya: recap: 1) dark canary for Q3a in private pool only (SE to coordinate) 2) share kernel/quant compatibility sheet 3) runbook with explicit fallback/egress language 4) customer benchmarks — two windows and traffic profile. we'll follow up in Slack and post the updated artifacts to the shared drive.
[16:02] Priya: thanks all.
[16:05] Ethan: thanks, we'll get the docs out.
[16:10] Maya: thanks everyone, talk soon.
[47:30] (meeting ended)

Notes: transcription includes occasional mis-hearings (e.g., "canary" sometimes transcribed as "canary" consistently) — please refer to attached artifacts for exact config snippets.
